title: A page for every season
text: Every season the league has played, 2008 to now, has its own page: final standings with seed, points rank, all-play record and luck, the playoff bracket, every matchup, that year's draft board, that year's trades, and 15 to 18 awards decided by the numbers. Reach them from History, or from any year on the Trophy Room page.

title: The title game, player by player
text: Each season page now shows both starting lineups from that year's championship side by side, every starter's points, and the duds flagged. Sixteen finals on record. Worth opening for 2013 alone, where a tight end who scored 13 touchdowns that season caught nothing at all in the final.

title: What the NFL was doing that year
text: Season pages now carry the real MVP and Offensive Rookie of the Year, plus the injuries, broken records and controversies that actually moved fantasy lineups that year. The NFL playoffs are left out on purpose: this league is finished before they start, so they never cost anybody a title.

title: The Yahoo years join everything
text: Trades, draft boards and season records now reach back to 2008 instead of stopping at 2014, and the 44 pre-2014 trades are graded like the rest. Teams whose manager was never identified win season awards like anyone else, but stay out of the all-time career lists, because any one of them could still turn out to belong to a manager who is still here.

title: Every team name you have ever used
text: Each manager page now lists every name that manager's team has gone by, oldest first, instead of hiding them in one league-wide table.

title: Real NFL headlines in the matchup write-ups
text: The weekly write-up for each matchup now pulls in the actual NFL news touching the players in those two lineups, so it can talk about what happened on Sunday instead of only the scores.

title: Record Watch
text: Which records can still fall this season and what each team needs, records already broken, and career milestones coming up. It sits at the top of the Record Book, on the home page, in the newsletter and on every manager page, and rebuilds itself from every game at each update.

title: The newsletter looks like a newspaper
text: A front page with a masthead, a standings ticker, the lead story in columns, an Inside this issue list and the week in numbers. Each matchup card now shows lead changes, the turning points, the playoff odds swing and who won each position.

title: This week's notes never go stale
text: The notes list on the Insights page now fills itself from the week's scores and ESPN headlines in any week the hand-written notes are missing.

title: Rivalry outlooks
text: Every rivalry page now opens with the story so far and where it stands this season: who leads, whether the series has changed hands, the next meeting and what a win would mean. It rewrites itself after every game.

title: Trade grade letters
text: Trade letters are now graded on a curve against every finished trade in the league, so the middle grades get used. Close trades are marked as fair, and a trade that cannot be judged yet says so.

title: Trophy Room and a Grades menu
text: Hall of Fame and Trophy Room are one page now, called Trophy Room. Trade Grades, Draft Grades and Waiver Returns have their own Grades group in the menu.

title: Player Hall of Fame
text: The Players page now has a Hall of Fame with written rules for getting in, a card for every player who made it, and a section for great players whose prime years were wasted here. The full player list can be sorted by any column and has headshots.

title: Football stats
text: Real yards, catches and touchdowns from the players each manager started, by season or all time, plus the biggest single games and longest plays ever put in a lineup.

title: Best-ever lineup and game log
text: Every manager page now shows that team's all-time starting lineup, its football totals with league rank, and a log of every game it has played.

title: Playoff race cards
text: Playoff Picture now opens with the race at a glance: spots, weeks left, who is in and who is out, and a card per team with the games left and its win-out record.

title: Rivalry Hub
text: Every head-to-head series now gets a rivalry score out of 100, with the league's biggest rivalry on top and tabs for the closest, the most played and the ones with a title game in them.

title: Career Leaders
text: All-time leader cards on the Hall of Fame page: titles, title games, playoff trips, playoff wins, wins, winning percentage and points.

title: Lineup Heat Map
text: Every starting lineup in the league on one grid. Green is a top starter at that spot, red is a weak one.

title: A letter on every draft pick
text: Draft Grades now shows each team's picks in a card, every pick graded against what that round usually returns.

title: What a pick is worth
text: Trade Grades now shows the average return of a pick in each round, and holds the grade on any trade with a pick that has not been used yet.

title: Power Lines
text: Every team's place in the standings, week by week, as crossing lines. Tap a name to trace one team, or drag the slider to rewind the season.

title: Rule Ideas page
text: A list of things other leagues do that we could try. Nothing on it is a rule, and nothing changes without a league vote.

title: Challenges page
text: Side games for next season: survivor, king of the hill, weekly high score and more. Nothing is running yet. Have a look and say which ones you would play.

title: Champions table
text: Every title game with the runner-up, third place and the final score, plus a tag when the finalist with the worse record won it.

title: Power rankings get a score
text: Each team now shows a 0 to 100 power score next to its bar. 50 is a league-average team. The ranking itself has not changed.

title: One Standings page
text: Power rankings, all-play, luck and lineup efficiency now sit on the Standings page as sections, with a jump-to row at the top. Three menu items are gone; nothing was removed.

title: Head-to-head grid on Rivalries
text: Every manager's record against every other manager on one grid. Green means the row leads the series, red means it trails. Tap a square for the full rivalry.

title: Jump to a section on long pages
text: Pages with four or more sections now start with a row of links, so you can go straight to the part you want.

title: Newsletters on the home page
text: The three latest issues sit right under this box, and each issue now ends with what is new on the site.

title: Playoff Picture
text: The seeds if the season ended today, how far every team is from the last spot, and which games left have a playoff place riding on them.

title: Rivalry pages show what kind of game each meeting was
text: Every meeting is tagged regular season, playoff or consolation, and the series record is split the same way. All of them still count.

title: Playoff odds that know your roster
text: Starting with the week 10 results, the odds and the weekly win chances read each team's current roster, injuries, byes and NFL matchups, not only what the team has scored so far.

title: This box
text: Additions and fixes to the site get listed here as they happen.

title: Trade matrix
text: A grid of how many trades every pair of managers has made. Tap a number to see those trades.

title: If the season ended today
text: Each weekly newsletter now shows the playoff field, the byes and the first-round games as the standings sit.

title: The what-if tracker
text: Each weekly newsletter tracks where the league would stand without kickers and with a league median game.
